subject: Startups
title: Net Revenue Retention
description: A quick win: understand Net Revenue Retention.

hook.text: What if your existing customers spent more every year—even without adding new ones? That's net revenue retention.

buildup.text: NRR measures how much revenue from existing customers grew or shrank over a year, including upsells and churn.

discovery.text: An NRR above 100% means expansion revenue exceeds losses. Snowflake hit 158% NRR—explosive organic growth.

twist.text: Below 100% means you're shrinking without new sales. Even growing companies can be dying underneath.

climax.text: NRR above 120% is world-class. It means the product gets stickier and more valuable over time.

punchline.text: Great products grow inside the customers they already have.

quiz.question: What does NRR above 100% indicate?
options: Existing customers are spending more than they churn
